name: multi-tenant-ecommerce-frontend
//: Security (sec.no_critical_cves): react-router and react-router-dom are pinned to the same exact patched release (7.18.5).
react-router-dom 7.x is a thin re-export of react-router, so both must resolve to one version. react-router 8.x requires React 19 and is incompatible with react@18 used here.

Releases before 6.30.3 / 7.12.0 carry HIGH open-redirect/XSS advisories (e.g. CVE-2026-22029), and 7.0.0-7.5.1 carry HIGH cache-poisoning/DoS advisories (CVE-2025-43864, CVE-2025-43865); 7.18.5 is outside all of these ranges.

@vitejs/plugin-react is held on 4.x because 6.x declares a vite ^8 peer dependency that conflicts with vite ^5 here; that conflict makes npm install fail with ERESOLVE, so the lockfile never picked up the react-router pin.

No overrides block is used: react-router-dom 7.18.5 depends on exactly react-router 7.18.5 and nothing else pulls react-router in, so the direct pin already yields a single copy. The previous self-referencing override was redundant and stopped npm from cleanly re-resolving the stale lockfile (which still held react-router 8.5.1 and @vitejs/plugin-react 6.x). Regenerate frontend/package-lock.json with npm install after this change.

Lockfile status: the committed frontend/package-lock.json still declared react-router ^6.30.6 and @vitejs/plugin-react ^6.2.1; it must be regenerated from this manifest with npm install so the installed versions are react-router/react-router-dom 7.18.5 and @vitejs/plugin-react 4.x. The frontend Docker build installs with npm ci, so the build fails if the lockfile drifts from this manifest again.

Accepted risk: if Trivy still reports a react-router CVE with no fixed version available, it is accepted for now because the app uses only declarative client-side routing (BrowserRouter/Routes/Route/Navigate) and no framework-mode SSR, loaders, actions or pre-rendering. Review date: 2027-02-04.
